title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
hook: With a language-cue interface, we find the grounding bottleneck is the coordinate output, not the model's ability to locate the evidence.

title: IKEA-Bench: Benchmarking and Mechanistic Analysis of Vision-Language Models for Cross-Depiction Assembly Instruction Alignment
hook: Adding text recovers instruction understanding but breaks diagram-to-video alignment. Scaling up does not help, because the bottleneck is the visual encoder.

title: NanoVDR: Distilling a 2B Vision-Language Retriever into a 70M Text-Only Encoder for Visual Document Retrieval
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP) 2026, Main Conference
hook: The query encoder does not need to see. A 70M text-only student keeps 95% of a 2B teacher's quality at 50x lower CPU latency.

title: ColNanoVDR: Document-Free Query Distillation for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval via Optimal Transport
hook: Multi-vector distillation does not need documents at all. Optimal transport aligns student and teacher query tokens, keeping 95% of teacher quality at 26x faster encoding.

title: DistilVDR: A Compact End-to-End Visual Document Retriever via Dual-Student Distillation
venue: Workshop on Document Intelligence and Understanding (DocInsights) at EMNLP 2026
hook: NanoVDR shrank only the query encoder. DistilVDR distills the whole retriever end-to-end from a single 8B teacher, keeping most of its quality at 524M with a 15x smaller index.

title: Structural Anchor Pruning: Training-Free Multi-Vector Compression for Visual Document Retrieval
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP) 2026, Main Conference
hook: A document's structure lives in the middle layers, not the final one. Pruning by that signal removes over 90% of the index without any training.

title: Inverting Multi-Vector Visual Document Indices
hook: A multi-vector index can be inverted back into readable pages. Shuffling the vectors does not stop it, but pooled indices stay substantially harder to invert.

title: Exploring Human-AI Collaboration in E-Textile Design: A Case Study on Flex Sensor Placement for Shoulder Motion Detection
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (PACM HCI) 2026, EICS
hook: LLM-assisted design does not help everyone equally. The least experienced designer improved through collaboration, the most experienced one regressed.

title: Mapping E-textiles Design Pain Points and Generative AI Opportunities: Insights from Workshops in Shanghai and Winchester
venue: International Conference on the Challenges, Opportunities, Innovations and Applications in Electronic Textiles (E-Textiles) 2026
hook: Two co-design workshops show the bottleneck in e-textile design is not model capability but the missing machine-readable formats that AI tools would need.

title: StrengthSense: A Dataset of IMU Signals Capturing Everyday Activities with Diverse Physical Demands
venue: Proceedings of the ACM International Symposium on Wearable Computers (ISWC) 2026
hook: An IMU dataset of everyday activities spanning a wide range of physical demands, for strength-aware activity recognition.

title: Knit-Structure Effects on Electromechanical Metrics and Their Correlation with Joint-Angle Estimation Error in Knitted Strain Sensors
hook: Knit structure drives gauge factor and baseline resistance, but uniaxial tests only screen out weak designs; joint-specific evaluation is still needed.

title: Encoder-Free Human Motion Understanding via Structured Motion Descriptions
hook: Human motion does not need an encoder. Describe it in structured words and let the LLM do the reasoning.

title: Fine-grained Motion Retrieval via Joint-Angle Motion Images and Token-Patch Late Interaction
hook: A 3D skeleton becomes a pseudo-image, so motion can be retrieved like a document, with token-level explainability.

title: LingoMotion: An Interpretable and Unambiguous Symbolic Representation for Human Motion
venue: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications (PerCom) 2026, Work-in-Progress
hook: Human motion gets its own alphabet, words and grammar, so the representation stays interpretable and unambiguous.
